transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I’m having a hard time staying with things I really need to focus on. Like I’ll start an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be sitting in a clinic metrics meeting fully intending to track what’s being said, and within a few minutes my mind is just… somewhere else. Then I’m rereading the same numbers over and over, or realizing I missed the main point of the discussion. It’s been frustrating, especially at work.
Have you noticed this kind of trouble focusing since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only become a problem recently?

No, it’s not just recent. I can remember it going back to elementary school. Teachers would write things like I was bright but careless, and my mom had to sit with me to get homework done because I’d lose track of what I was supposed to do, or I’d forget books at school. So it feels like it’s been there a long time—it’s just more obvious now with work.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about various things—like work, health, or family—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about work like anyone does, especially when I’m behind or something is important, but it doesn’t feel like I’m worrying all day for no reason. I wouldn’t say it’s more days than not.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling persistently down, sad, or losing interest and pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

No, not really. I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently sad or down. I still enjoy things when I actually get to them. I’m mostly frustrated with myself at times, but I don’t think I’ve lost interest in things overall.
Do you notice similar trouble focusing or staying organized in other areas of your life, like at home, managing finances, or in social situations—not just at work?

Yes, it’s not only at work. At home I can get behind on bills or paperwork because I put it off and then lose track of it. And with the volunteer health workshops I’ve helped with, I actually had to step back from leading parts of the planning because I couldn’t reliably keep all the pieces moving. At work it’s been affecting clinic reporting deadlines too, and other teams end up waiting on me, which is pretty embarrassing.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively without thinking things through?

I don’t think that’s really me. I’m not especially restless or fidgety, and I don’t usually have trouble sitting still. I also don’t think I interrupt people much or act impulsively. My issues feel more like… keeping track of things and staying focused, not being physically restless.
Have you been sleeping well lately—getting enough restful sleep most nights—and do you use alcohol, caffeine, or any recreational drugs regularly?

I’m not really sure there’s anything major to report there. My sleep seems okay overall, I think, and I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with alcohol, caffeine, or drugs. I don’t use recreational drugs.
Do you often misplace or lose things you need for daily tasks—like your keys, phone, or important documents—or forget appointments and errands you meant to do?

Yes, that happens a lot. I’m constantly looking for things I need—my badge, handwritten notes, clinic folders. Sometimes even a flash drive I swear I just had in my hand before a meeting. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I used to be the organized one.
Thinking back to childhood, were you ever notably hyperactive, impulsive, or unable to stay seated—more than other kids your age—even if that's not how you are now?

I’m not really sure. I don’t remember being especially hyperactive or the kid who couldn’t stay seated. I’d have to think more or maybe ask someone who knew me then, but nothing like that really stands out to me.
